Summary
The Managing Director of Policy at AAPI Equity Alliance leads policy and advocacy efforts for the organization’s core issue areas and supports its members and committees. They also co-lead the policy team at Stop AAPI Hate, a U.S. based coalition advocating for racial justice and the largest center tracking acts of hate against Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders nationwide.

The Managing Director of Policy is a key member of AAPI Equity Alliance and Stop AAPI Hate leadership teams, driving decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic direction for the organization and coalition.

Key Responsibilities
Essential responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Lead and Manage Policy Team

Responsible for providing direction, guidance, and support to the Director of Government Affairs and the Director of Federal Policy. This includes fostering a collaborative and productive

work environment, promoting professional development, and addressing any team challenges.
Develop and articulate a clear strategic vision for the Policy Team, ensuring alignment with the organization's overall goals and objectives. Responsible for managing the team's resources effectively, including budget allocation, staffing decisions, and the procurement of necessary tools and technologies.
As a member of the management team at AAPI Equity Alliance act as the representative for the activities and needs of the Policy Team.

Analysis of Local, State, and Federal Policy and Practice

Monitor policy and practice environments on issue areas and identify opportunities for AAPI Equity Alliance to respond and contribute to developments in the sector
Develop and contribute to written research briefs, reports, statements, letters of support/opposition, and proposed bill language in alignment with policy priorities; develop other tools and resources that make complex data and information accessible to a broad array of stakeholders
Research and analyze policy and practice at Los Angeles county, state, and federal Levels

External Relations and Coalition-Building

Work collaboratively with advocacy and community partners and coalitions to maximize AAPI Equity Alliance’s impact
Develop and execute campaigns that strengthen coalitions and deepen AAPI Equity Alliance’s relationships with advocacy and partners
Advocate for AAPI Equity Alliance’s position on key issues by representing AAPI Equity Alliance in external meetings and developing relationships with key stakeholders and partners

Skills and Abilities
Law degree (JD) and bachelor’s degree in public policy, social work, public health or a related field
At least 9-12 years of experience working in policy, legislative, advocacy, or government affairs
Superb communication skills, including the ability to clearly and impactfully communicate AAPI Equity Alliance and Stop AAPI Hate’s positions, and quickly establish credibility and rapport
Proactive, self-motivated problem solver who can take initiative, balance multiple priorities simultaneously, and use sound judgment in ambiguous, fast-changing, and unpredictable environments
Excellent interpersonal skills, including proven ability to work effectively both in person and remotely with teammates and a diverse set of stakeholder
True team player with excellent teamwork and collaboration skills; willing to support team members as needed across the organization for high-priority projects or events
Strong analytical, research, and verbal and written communication skills, with an emphasis on an ability to effectively communicate with diverse audiences across media platforms
Outstanding organizational and project management skills, with impeccable attention to detail and ability to work under pressure with a high degree of accuracy
Solid background in information technology, including proficiency in MS Office, G- Suite, Zoom, and Slack
Ability to work flexible hours which include some evenings and weekends
Knowledge of cultural norms and nuances affecting Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) communities
Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of AAPI Equity Alliance and Stop AAPI Hate

About AAPI Equity Alliance
AAPI Equity Alliance is dedicated to improving the lives of AAPIs through civic engagement, capacity building, and policy advocacy. Learn more at https://aapiequityalliance.org.

About Stop AAPI Hate
Stop AAPI Hate is a U.S.-based coalition dedicated to ending racism and discrimination against Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders (AAs & PIs). We strive to advance the multiracial movement for equity and justice by building power for our communities, working in solidarity with other communities of color, and advocating for comprehensive solutions that tackle the root causes of race-based hate. As the nation’s largest reporting center tracking anti-AAPI hate acts, our coalition publishes data insights and research findings to paint a vivid and nuanced picture of racism and other forms of bigotry as it is experienced by our communities. Leveraging our core strategies – Data & Research, Policy & Advocacy, Community Capacity Building, and Narrative Change – we drive progress across three distinct issue areas to create a safer, more equitable future for all. Learn more at https://stopaapihate.org.

To Apply
Please email a cover letter, resume, and 3-5 page writing sample in one pdf to info@aapiequityalliance.org. In the subject line, please write “Managing Director of Policy.” 
Benefits
Benefits include paid vacation and sick leave, reimbursement for health and dental insurance, and a budget for technology. T his position is currently hybrid . Position available immediately.

With offices nationwide, the firm serves organizations around the world as an independent member of Nexia.

We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a Director/Managing Director, AI Software Development
to support our Global Digital & CyberSecurity
practice.

CohnReznick is a hybrid firm and most of our professionals are located within a commutable distance to one of our offices. This position is considered remote which means it does not require job duties be performed within proximity of a CohnReznick office location. However, as a remote employee, you may be required to be present at a CohnReznick office with scheduled notice for client work, team meetings, or trainings.

YOUR TEAM.

The Director / Managing Director, AI Software Development is a senior technology leader responsible for establishing and leading CohnReznick's software engineering capability. This position defines the vision, strategy, operating model, talent plan, architecture, and delivery approach for AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions across the firm.

The position is accountable for building a high-performing AI-native software development organization capable of delivering proprietary technology assets that create sustainable competitive advantage. The leader oversees the design, development, deployment, and operation of AI-powered applications, intelligent automation solutions, agentic workflows, and client-facing digital products.

This is not a traditional application-development leadership role. The successful candidate must have personally built and scaled a native AI software team from inception through production delivery, including recruiting specialized talent, establishing engineering and governance standards, and delivering secure applications with measurable business impact.

WHY COHNREZNICK?

At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. Whether it’s working alongside your peers to solve a client challenge, or volunteering together at the local food bank, there are so many ways to find your “why” at the firm.

We believe it’s important to balance work with everyday life – and make time for enjoyment and fun. We invest in a robust Total Rewards package that includes everything from generous PTO, a flexible work environment, expanded parental leave, extensive learning & development, and even paid time off for employees to volunteer.

YOUR ROLE.

Responsibilities Include But Not Limited To

AI strategy and portfolio leadership

Define and execute a multi-year AI software engineering strategy aligned with firm business and technology objectives.
Establish the vision, roadmap, investment priorities, and operating model for the GDC AI development capability.
Identify opportunities to create proprietary software assets that improve client service, quality, efficiency, growth, and professional experience.
Advise executive leaders and governance forums on opportunities, investments, risks, dependencies, and portfolio performance.

Native AI organization building

Recruit, organize, develop, and retain a multidisciplinary team of AI engineers, software engineers, machine learning engineers, technical leads, and architects.
Define job architecture, role expectations, career paths, leadership spans, technical communities, and talent-development practices for the AI engineering function.
Create an engineering culture centered on innovation, responsible experimentation, accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and disciplined production delivery.
Build a sustainable talent pipeline and develop future engineering leaders.

Product and solution delivery

Lead AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions from discovery and architecture through engineering, release, adoption, operation, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Product Management and business stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into sequenced, funded, and measurable delivery commitments.
Manage execution across concurrent initiatives while balancing value, speed, quality, security, risk, reliability, and maintainability.
Establish outcome, delivery, quality, adoption, and operational measures; use results to improve priorities and execution.

Architecture, engineering, and operations

Establish development standards, reference architectures, engineering frameworks, reusable components, testing practices, and technical quality controls.
Define patterns for large language model integration, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent workflow automation, observability, evaluation, and model operations.
Implement modern cloud-native engineering, DevSecOps, CI/CD, API, integration, reliability, incident-management, and lifecycle-management practices.
Promote reuse, platform leverage, technical-debt management, and reduction of unnecessary technology redundancy.

Governance, risk, and stakeholder leadership

Embed security, privacy, legal, regulatory, records-management, data-governance, and responsible AI requirements throughout the development lifecycle.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Data & Analytics, Risk, Legal, and other control functions to govern design and deployment decisions.
Communicate complex technical matters in clear business terms and build trusted relationships with executives, professionals, clients, vendors, and strategic partners.
Drive adoption, change leadership, knowledge transfer, and transparent reporting of progress, risks, decisions, and realized value.

The duties listed are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. They are not an exhaustive list of every responsibility, duty, or skill required. Responsibilities may change based on business needs.

Your Experience.

The successful candidate will have:

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Fifteen or more years of progressive software engineering and technology leadership experience.
Seven or more years leading software development organizations, including leaders of engineering teams.
Five or more years delivering AI-enabled applications, machine learning platforms, intelligent automation solutions, or generative AI products.
Demonstrated success creating and scaling a native AI software development organization that moved beyond pilots and experimentation to secure, production-grade solutions.
Proven delivery of enterprise-grade software products and platforms in complex, regulated, or high-trust environments.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and a blended workforce of employees, contractors, and strategic partners.

Technical and delivery expertise

Generative AI, large language models, agentic architectures, retrieval-augmented generation, AI evaluation, observability, and model operations.
Cloud-native software development, enterprise application architecture, APIs, integration patterns, data platforms, and analytics ecosystems.
DevSecOps, CI/CD, automated testing, software supply-chain controls, production reliability, and secure development lifecycle practices.
Responsible AI, AI governance, privacy, security, model risk, data governance, and human oversight.
Product-oriented delivery using measurable outcomes, iterative development, user feedback, adoption measures, and value realization.

Preferred Qualifications

Leadership experience in professional services, financial services, regulated industries, or enterprise B2B software.
Experience with Microsoft Azure AI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot technologies, and modern AI engineering frameworks.

jobs.title: Executive Director  - Animal Protection Society of Durham
jobs.description:
Career Opportunity

The Animal Protection Society of Durham (APS) seeks a steady, strategic, and relationship-centered leader to serve as its next Executive Director. The ideal candidate will build on recent organizational progress, strengthen people and systems, cultivate trusting partnerships, and translate APS's mission into clear, measurable priorities for the future.

Looking ahead, APS is exploring the development of a new shelter facility that would better support animal care, community services, and the organization’s long-term growth. The next Executive Director will have an opportunity to help shape the vision, partnerships, funding strategy, and planning required to bring this transformational project forward.

Mission:
We strengthen bonds between people and animals in Durham County through community engagement and compassionate care for animals in need.

Reporting Structure:
The Executive Director reports to a nine-member Board of Directors and currently leads seven direct reports overseeing lifesaving programs, animal well-being and medical services, facilities and animal care, development and communications, behavior, foster and rescue, and community engagement.

Scope:
Approximately 30 staff members and an annual operating budget of approximately $3 million. APS’s work is also supported by hundreds of volunteers and foster caregivers, who contributed nearly 22,000 hours of service in FY2025.

Compensation:
The anticipated salary range for this position is $120,000-$145,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. APS also offers a competitive benefits package with additional details to be shared with candidates during the search process.

Working Environment/Location:
This is an on-site leadership position based in Durham, North Carolina. The Executive Director is expected to maintain a visible presence with staff, volunteers, animals, public-sector partners, donors, and the community.

Key Responsibilities of the Executive Director

Organizational Leadership and Culture

Lead APS through the completion of its organizational stabilization and into its next phase of sustainable growth and strategic development.
Build on recent progress in communication, transparency, cross-departmental collaboration, and accountability while fostering a shared sense of one APS team.
Strengthen the leadership and management capacity of directors and supervisors through clear expectations, coaching, delegation, and consistent performance management.
Support a healthy workplace culture that recognizes the emotional demands of animal welfare work and promotes staff well-being, retention, professional growth, and resilience.

Strategy, Operations, and Organizational Effectiveness

Partner with the Board and staff to establish clear short- and long-term strategic priorities and translate them into annual plans, measurable outcomes, and organizational accountability.
Ensure consistent, effective operations across sheltering, medical care, intake, foster care, behavior, adoption, community programs, and administrative functions.
Continue strengthening organizational systems, policies, technology, financial controls, safety practices, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Balance the urgency inherent in an open-admission shelter environment with disciplined prioritization and systems that reduce reliance on crisis response.

Animal Welfare and Program Impact

Ensure APS delivers humane, high-quality, evidence-informed care and remains responsive to evolving best practices in animal welfare.
Partner closely with APS veterinary, behavior, shelter operations, foster, and lifesaving professionals, appropriately relying on their technical expertise.
Establish clear organizational priorities around intake, capacity for care, animal outcomes, foster care, rescue partnerships, prevention, and community services.
Expand APS' ability to keep animals with their families when appropriate and leverage foster homes, volunteers, rescue partners, and community-based services to improve outcomes.

Community, Government, and Strategic Relationships

Serve as a visible, credible ambassador for APS throughout Durham and the broader animal welfare community.
Maintain and deepen the critical partnership among APS, Durham County Government, Animal Services, the Durham County Sheriff's Office, and regulatory partners.
Build constructive relationships with volunteers, rescue organizations, veterinary providers, donors, community organizations, and other stakeholders.
Strengthen APS's reputation through transparency, responsiveness, consistent performance, and clear communication - particularly when navigating difficult decisions or changing practices

Financial Leadership, Fundraising, and Governance

Maintain strong stewardship of APS's financial resources through sound budgeting, forecasting, controls, reporting, and greater departmental ownership of budgets.
Partner actively with the Director of Development and Communications to strengthen donor engagement, diversify revenue, and grow annual, major, planned, corporate, and foundation giving.
Develop a strong, transparent partnership with the Board of Directors, providing the information and strategic context needed for effective governance and organizational oversight.
Clarify and reinforce appropriate distinctions between governance and management while engaging Board members in strategy, fundraising, advocacy, and key external relationships.

The Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will possess many of the following qualifications and attributes:
Significant senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, public-serving, or similarly complex mission-driven organization, including demonstrated success leading through change, transition, stabilization, or growth.
Experience with facility planning, capital campaigns, or other significant organizational growth initiatives is preferred.
A strong people leader who develops others, establishes clear expectations, addresses difficult issues, and creates accountability while maintaining trust and respect.
Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to listen, synthesize differing perspectives, make decisions, explain the rationale, and follow through consistently.
Strong operational, financial, and systems-management skills, including the ability to prioritize effectively, delegate appropriately, use data to inform decisions, and strengthen organizational infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to build productive partnerships with governing boards, public agencies, regulators, donors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Direct animal welfare or sheltering experience is preferred but not required. Candidates without significant direct experience must demonstrate genuine commitment to animal welfare, learning agility, sound judgment, respect for technical expertise, and the ability to quickly understand the complexities of open-admission sheltering.
A steady, resilient, humble, and strategic leader who is skilled in change management, comfortable making difficult decisions, and able to maintain appropriate visibility in day-to-day operations while staying focused on executive-level responsibilities.

About Animal Protection Society of Durham

Founded in 1970, the Animal Protection Society of Durham is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening the bond between people and animals. Since 1990, APS has managed the Durham County Animal Shelter in partnership with Durham County Government. APS operates Durham County's only open-admission animal shelter and provides care to thousands of vulnerable animals each year.

Beyond sheltering and adoption, APS provides and supports foster care, community spay/neuter, behavioral services, pet food and supply assistance, rescue partnerships, medical care, and other programs designed to help animals and the people who care for them. APS is entering an important next chapter, with the opportunity to build on recent progress in operations, culture, animal care, partnerships, and accountability while defining its long-term role in Durham's animal welfare ecosystem.

Want to know more? Visit www.apsofdurham.org.

About Durham

Durham is one of North Carolina’s most dynamic and fast-growing communities. Home to more than 305,000 residents , the city has grown nearly 8% since 2020, and more than 57% of adults hold a bachelor’s degree or higher. Durham is anchored by Duke University, North Carolina Central University, world-class healthcare institutions, and Research Triangle Park, a 7,000-acre innovation hub that is home to more than 385 companies.

Durham’s quality of life has also earned national attention. Forbes included Raleigh-Durham among the nation’s top 15 communities for quality of life, Livability named Durham one of the best places to live in the United States in 2025, and Food & Wine recognized it as one of “America’s next great food cities.” The community also offers nationally recognized arts and entertainment, diverse neighborhoods, outdoor recreation, and a strong tradition of civic engagement.

This combination of rapid growth, innovation, diversity, and community commitment gives APS’s next leader a meaningful platform for partnership and impact. It also creates increasingly complex animal welfare needs as Durham works to ensure that services remain accessible to animals and the people who care for them.

Want to know more? Visit www.discoverdurham.com.

Benefits

APS offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees, including generous health coverage, retirement contributions, paid time off, and professional development opportunities. We are committed to providing benefits and workplace practices that support employee well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

How To Apply

Job ID:
LP_00023575-2660487

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

The Executive Director of Advanced Practice is a strategic and operational leader, responsible for optimizing the delivery of care provided by all Nurse Practitioners (NPs), Physician Assistants (PAs), Certified Nurse Midwives (CNMs), Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs), Genetic Counselors (GC) within LPCH/SMCH Center for Advanced Practice (CAP). This Executive Director serves to set strategic vision and drive the purpose of the Center for Advanced Practice in alignment with the mission, vision, and values of the greater organization.

The Executive Director will advance the professional practice environment by ensuring clinically competent Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) represent the organization in healthcare delivery through patient care, research, training, and education. The Executive Director will be responsible for establishing APP scope of practice to ensure full practice authority where appropriate. The Executive Director will establish APP productivity and utilization standards and drive revenue maximization as they relate to APP direct clinical work (consider: governance and accountability, role architecture and standard expectations, APP deployment and clinical integration, measurement systems that capture direct and indirect contributions, talent and career development, workforce economics and strategic planning.

The Executive Director is responsible for staying up to date on all clinical and regulatory requirements and leads the execution of those requirements across the enterprise.

The Executive Director fills an executive sponsorship role where they partner with key constituents across the enterprise to represent the Center for Advanced Practice. They actively contribute to strategic decisions to ensure that those decisions align with the Center for Advanced Practice strategic mission and vision.

Examples of key partnerships could include but are not limited to divisions, human resources, marketing, medical staffing, finance, strategy, process improvement, quality improvement, academic clinical partnerships, and a variety of other clinical, operational, and strategic committees.

Essential Functions

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.

Employees must abide by all Joint Commission Requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, patient care, patient rights and ethical treatment, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety and quality programs, sustaining compliance with National Patient Safety Goals, and licensure and health screenings.

Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the hospital's policies and procedures, including its Service Standards and its Code of Conduct.

Professsional/Personal Development

Identifies specific needs for self-development and implements a plan to achieve professional growth and networking.
Promotes the professional growth and development of CAP leaders through coaching, mentoring and support and creates guidelines and financial resources for professional growth, education and research.
Promotes and supports APP leader professional goals for regional, national and international professional practice including attending conferences, presenting at conferences, conducting research and generating publications.

Strategic Leadership

Leads in the development, execution, and revision of CAP strategic plan.
Leads annual goal development, deployment, and measurement process.

Management Team

Oversees CAP organizational structure, meeting agenda and facilitation, and drives an environment that facilitates collaboration and participation.
Develops and sustains an empowered, high-performing CAP leadership team through transparent communication, shared decision-making, appropriate delegation, and participation in strategic and operational decision-making.
Sponsors process improvement initiatives led by CAP leadership to achieve and maintain quality patient care.
Assigns special projects and designates committee assignments to APP leaders and ensures support and resources for project goals.

Skills

Leads and role models behaviors that foster diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Cap Initiatives

Determines the need for professional practice advisory taskforces to prioritize projects, facilitate problem-solving, delegate tasks, and improve communication to support CAP initiatives.
Uses a systematic process to effectively plan, implement, and evaluate new programs in conjunction with division/service physicians and hospital and clinic leadership.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration

Establishes and maintains collaborative working relationships with hospital and service line leadership, medical staff, and all members of the patient care team.
Serves as the leader, positive role model, and effective liaison for Stanford Medicine Children's Health (SMCH) and key external stakeholders.
Is actively involved with governmental agencies, professional organizations, health policy/advocacy groups to identify and implement best practices in professional practice and pediatric healthcare.

Operations

Financial:

Assures the delivery of quality and cost-effective patient care by working collaboratively with the APPs and GCs in ambulatory and inpatient settings.
Oversees APP billing practices in conjunction with the Provider Enrollment and Compliance Departments, as well as with physician practices.
Establishes and maintains patient care, human resources, systems, and workflow processes, including the development, review, and annual update of the CAP budget.

Data Collection And Analysis

Demonstrates the ability to collect, analyze and synthesize clinical, financial and outcomes data for effective decision making.

Human Resources

Designs strategy to ensure the availability and retention of high-quality human resources for APP services, to include overseeing the development/revision of job descriptions by the CAP leadership team and working with Human Resources to maintain a competitive compensation strategy.

CAP Leadership Team

Oversees CAP leadership team to collaborate with faculty, patient care directors, practice and site managers, service line leaders, nursing staff and support services to determine staffing standards and assuring the appropriate number of APP staff; assessing scheduling practices based on service requirements.
Oversees the operations, strategy, and business needs to lead a team CAP leaders to support the clinical and professional practice of advanced practice professionals across the continuum.
Advocates for space and other resources needed by CAP.

Productivity And Utilization

Establishes APP productivity guidelines and engages in strategic planning for implementation and utilization of these guidelines in accordance with CAP and organizational strategic vision.
Leads strategies to optimize APP contribution to patient access, aligning APP utilization, deployment and practice models with SMCH access initiatives and organizational goals.
Guides the management team to create, maintain, and update staffing models to ensure appropriate staffing across all units and specialties.
Oversees the management team to review all new and replacement APP positions supporting resource stewardship and ensuring patient care needs are met.

Professional Practice

Identification of system and service specific clinical performance goals. Development and adherence to policies relative to APP practice. Development and implementation of best practice integrated care models.
Oversees credentialing and privileging competencies for the professional staff and participation in peer review.
Develops and maintains policies and procedures relating to the practice of the APPs.
Ensures compliance with the State Board of Nursing/ Physician Assistant Board and other state regulations.
Non-voting member of the Medical Executive Committee, reviews and approves Advanced Health Practitioner (AHP) files as related to the organization’s credentialing process.

Recruitment & Retention

Strategically oversees programs which address APP Recruitment and retention.
Collaborates with marketing for both internal and external CAP marketing opportunities.

Advocacy

Educates and advocates on appropriate utilization of APPs in and across the system. Promotes interdisciplinary practice and implements strategies to overcome barriers to collaboration.
Demonstrates national leadership presence by engaging in scholarly work such as presentations and publications.
Partners with other state leaders in advocacy efforts for advanced practice.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities as well as possession of any required licenses or certifications is qualifying.

Education

Master's degree in a related field from an accredited university required. Doctorate preferred and/or additional leadership training.

Experience

Five (5) years of broad and extensive experience managing and leading programs, work units or departments of comparable size, scope and complexity.

Ten (10) years of clinical experience as an APP.

License/Certification

Multispecialty leadership experience preferred.

CA Registered Nurse - valid license as a Registered Nurse issued by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN) (required within 2 months of hire for candidates outside of California. Clinical Supervision allowed only after obtaining California license)

- AND -

NP - Certification to practice as a Nurse Practitioner through the California Board of Registered Nursing, NP Board Certification (required within 2 months of hire for candidates outside of California. Clinical Supervision allowed only after obtaining California license).

Certification as a Nurse Practitioner by a nationally accredited nursing organization (e.g. American Association of Nurse Practitioners - AANP, American Nurses Credentialing Center ' ANCC, Pediatric Nursing Certification Board - PNCB or any successor organizations) is required.

- OR -

CA Physician Assistant - Valid license as a Physician Assistant in CA, PA national board certification.

Attributes/Skills

These are the observable and measurable attributes and skills required to perform successfully the essential functions of the job and are generally demonstrated through qualifying experience, education or licensure/certification.

Strong clinical practice skills.
Ability to provide effective staff supervision, including planning and assigning work according to the nature of the job to be accomplished, the capabilities of subordinates and available resources; controlling work through periodic reviews and/or evaluations; determining subordinates' training needs and arranging for such training; Motivating subordinates to work effectively; determining the need for disciplinary action and either recommending or initiating disciplinary action.

Job Description

CohnReznick helps organizations optimize performance, manage risk, and maximize value through CohnReznick LLP (assurance services) and CohnReznick Advisory LLC (advisory and tax services). Together, the firm provides leaders with deep industry knowledge and relationships, solutions to address clients’ unique business goals and risks, and insight on how emerging market forces can drive opportunity. With offices nationwide, the firm serves organizations around the world as an independent member of Nexia.

We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a Director/Managing Director, AI Software Development
to support our Global Digital & CyberSecurity
practice.

CohnReznick is a hybrid firm and most of our professionals are located within a commutable distance to one of our offices. This position is considered remote which means it does not require job duties be performed within proximity of a CohnReznick office location. However, as a remote employee, you may be required to be present at a CohnReznick office with scheduled notice for client work, team meetings, or trainings.

YOUR TEAM.

The Director / Managing Director, AI Software Development is a senior technology leader responsible for establishing and leading CohnReznick's software engineering capability. This position defines the vision, strategy, operating model, talent plan, architecture, and delivery approach for AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions across the firm.

The position is accountable for building a high-performing AI-native software development organization capable of delivering proprietary technology assets that create sustainable competitive advantage. The leader oversees the design, development, deployment, and operation of AI-powered applications, intelligent automation solutions, agentic workflows, and client-facing digital products.

This is not a traditional application-development leadership role. The successful candidate must have personally built and scaled a native AI software team from inception through production delivery, including recruiting specialized talent, establishing engineering and governance standards, and delivering secure applications with measurable business impact.

WHY COHNREZNICK?

At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. Whether it’s working alongside your peers to solve a client challenge, or volunteering together at the local food bank, there are so many ways to find your “why” at the firm.

We believe it’s important to balance work with everyday life – and make time for enjoyment and fun. We invest in a robust Total Rewards package that includes everything from generous PTO, a flexible work environment, expanded parental leave, extensive learning & development, and even paid time off for employees to volunteer.

YOUR ROLE.

Responsibilities Include But Not Limited To

AI strategy and portfolio leadership

Define and execute a multi-year AI software engineering strategy aligned with firm business and technology objectives.
Establish the vision, roadmap, investment priorities, and operating model for the GDC AI development capability.
Identify opportunities to create proprietary software assets that improve client service, quality, efficiency, growth, and professional experience.
Advise executive leaders and governance forums on opportunities, investments, risks, dependencies, and portfolio performance.

Native AI organization building

Recruit, organize, develop, and retain a multidisciplinary team of AI engineers, software engineers, machine learning engineers, technical leads, and architects.
Define job architecture, role expectations, career paths, leadership spans, technical communities, and talent-development practices for the AI engineering function.
Create an engineering culture centered on innovation, responsible experimentation, accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and disciplined production delivery.
Build a sustainable talent pipeline and develop future engineering leaders.

Product and solution delivery

Lead AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions from discovery and architecture through engineering, release, adoption, operation, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Product Management and business stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into sequenced, funded, and measurable delivery commitments.
Manage execution across concurrent initiatives while balancing value, speed, quality, security, risk, reliability, and maintainability.
Establish outcome, delivery, quality, adoption, and operational measures; use results to improve priorities and execution.

Architecture, engineering, and operations

Establish development standards, reference architectures, engineering frameworks, reusable components, testing practices, and technical quality controls.
Define patterns for large language model integration, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent workflow automation, observability, evaluation, and model operations.
Implement modern cloud-native engineering, DevSecOps, CI/CD, API, integration, reliability, incident-management, and lifecycle-management practices.
Promote reuse, platform leverage, technical-debt management, and reduction of unnecessary technology redundancy.

Governance, risk, and stakeholder leadership

Embed security, privacy, legal, regulatory, records-management, data-governance, and responsible AI requirements throughout the development lifecycle.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Data & Analytics, Risk, Legal, and other control functions to govern design and deployment decisions.
Communicate complex technical matters in clear business terms and build trusted relationships with executives, professionals, clients, vendors, and strategic partners.
Drive adoption, change leadership, knowledge transfer, and transparent reporting of progress, risks, decisions, and realized value.

The duties listed are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. They are not an exhaustive list of every responsibility, duty, or skill required. Responsibilities may change based on business needs.

Your Experience.

The successful candidate will have:

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Fifteen or more years of progressive software engineering and technology leadership experience.
Seven or more years leading software development organizations, including leaders of engineering teams.
Five or more years delivering AI-enabled applications, machine learning platforms, intelligent automation solutions, or generative AI products.
Demonstrated success creating and scaling a native AI software development organization that moved beyond pilots and experimentation to secure, production-grade solutions.
Proven delivery of enterprise-grade software products and platforms in complex, regulated, or high-trust environments.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and a blended workforce of employees, contractors, and strategic partners.

Technical and delivery expertise

Generative AI, large language models, agentic architectures, retrieval-augmented generation, AI evaluation, observability, and model operations.
Cloud-native software development, enterprise application architecture, APIs, integration patterns, data platforms, and analytics ecosystems.
DevSecOps, CI/CD, automated testing, software supply-chain controls, production reliability, and secure development lifecycle practices.
Responsible AI, AI governance, privacy, security, model risk, data governance, and human oversight.
Product-oriented delivery using measurable outcomes, iterative development, user feedback, adoption measures, and value realization.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Business, or a related field.
Leadership experience in professional services, financial services, regulated industries, or enterprise B2B software.
Experience with Microsoft Azure AI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot technologies, and modern AI engineering frameworks.
Relevant credentials in AI, cloud architecture, software engineering, cybersecurity, or product delivery.
Experience commercializing proprietary software or creating client-facing digital products and technology-enabled services.

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

The Executive Director reports to a nine-member Board of Directors and currently leads seven direct reports overseeing lifesaving programs, animal well-being and medical services, facilities and animal care, development and communications, behavior, foster and rescue, and community engagement.

Scope:
Approximately 30 staff members and an annual operating budget of approximately $3 million. APS’s work is also supported by hundreds of volunteers and foster caregivers, who contributed nearly 22,000 hours of service in FY2025.

Compensation:
The anticipated salary range for this position is $120,000-$145,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. APS also offers a competitive benefits package with additional details to be shared with candidates during the search process.

Working Environment/Location:
This is an on-site leadership position based in Durham, North Carolina. The Executive Director is expected to maintain a visible presence with staff, volunteers, animals, public-sector partners, donors, and the community.

Key Responsibilities of the Executive Director

Organizational Leadership and Culture

Lead APS through the completion of its organizational stabilization and into its next phase of sustainable growth and strategic development.
Build on recent progress in communication, transparency, cross-departmental collaboration, and accountability while fostering a shared sense of one APS team.
Strengthen the leadership and management capacity of directors and supervisors through clear expectations, coaching, delegation, and consistent performance management.
Support a healthy workplace culture that recognizes the emotional demands of animal welfare work and promotes staff well-being, retention, professional growth, and resilience.

Strategy, Operations, and Organizational Effectiveness

Partner with the Board and staff to establish clear short- and long-term strategic priorities and translate them into annual plans, measurable outcomes, and organizational accountability.
Ensure consistent, effective operations across sheltering, medical care, intake, foster care, behavior, adoption, community programs, and administrative functions.
Continue strengthening organizational systems, policies, technology, financial controls, safety practices, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Balance the urgency inherent in an open-admission shelter environment with disciplined prioritization and systems that reduce reliance on crisis response.

Animal Welfare and Program Impact

Ensure APS delivers humane, high-quality, evidence-informed care and remains responsive to evolving best practices in animal welfare.
Partner closely with APS veterinary, behavior, shelter operations, foster, and lifesaving professionals, appropriately relying on their technical expertise.
Establish clear organizational priorities around intake, capacity for care, animal outcomes, foster care, rescue partnerships, prevention, and community services.
Expand APS' ability to keep animals with their families when appropriate and leverage foster homes, volunteers, rescue partners, and community-based services to improve outcomes.

Community, Government, and Strategic Relationships

Serve as a visible, credible ambassador for APS throughout Durham and the broader animal welfare community.
Maintain and deepen the critical partnership among APS, Durham County Government, Animal Services, the Durham County Sheriff's Office, and regulatory partners.
Build constructive relationships with volunteers, rescue organizations, veterinary providers, donors, community organizations, and other stakeholders.
Strengthen APS's reputation through transparency, responsiveness, consistent performance, and clear communication - particularly when navigating difficult decisions or changing practices

Financial Leadership, Fundraising, and Governance

Maintain strong stewardship of APS's financial resources through sound budgeting, forecasting, controls, reporting, and greater departmental ownership of budgets.
Partner actively with the Director of Development and Communications to strengthen donor engagement, diversify revenue, and grow annual, major, planned, corporate, and foundation giving.
Develop a strong, transparent partnership with the Board of Directors, providing the information and strategic context needed for effective governance and organizational oversight.
Clarify and reinforce appropriate distinctions between governance and management while engaging Board members in strategy, fundraising, advocacy, and key external relationships.

The Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will possess many of the following qualifications and attributes:
Significant senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, public-serving, or similarly complex mission-driven organization, including demonstrated success leading through change, transition, stabilization, or growth.
Experience with facility planning, capital campaigns, or other significant organizational growth initiatives is preferred.
A strong people leader who develops others, establishes clear expectations, addresses difficult issues, and creates accountability while maintaining trust and respect.
Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to listen, synthesize differing perspectives, make decisions, explain the rationale, and follow through consistently.
Strong operational, financial, and systems-management skills, including the ability to prioritize effectively, delegate appropriately, use data to inform decisions, and strengthen organizational infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to build productive partnerships with governing boards, public agencies, regulators, donors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Direct animal welfare or sheltering experience is preferred but not required. Candidates without significant direct experience must demonstrate genuine commitment to animal welfare, learning agility, sound judgment, respect for technical expertise, and the ability to quickly understand the complexities of open-admission sheltering.
A steady, resilient, humble, and strategic leader who is skilled in change management, comfortable making difficult decisions, and able to maintain appropriate visibility in day-to-day operations while staying focused on executive-level responsibilities.

About Animal Protection Society of Durham

Founded in 1970, the Animal Protection Society of Durham is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening the bond between people and animals. Since 1990, APS has managed the Durham County Animal Shelter in partnership with Durham County Government. APS operates Durham County's only open-admission animal shelter and provides care to thousands of vulnerable animals each year.

Beyond sheltering and adoption, APS provides and supports foster care, community spay/neuter, behavioral services, pet food and supply assistance, rescue partnerships, medical care, and other programs designed to help animals and the people who care for them. APS is entering an important next chapter, with the opportunity to build on recent progress in operations, culture, animal care, partnerships, and accountability while defining its long-term role in Durham's animal welfare ecosystem.

Want to know more? Visit www.apsofdurham.org.

About Durham

Durham is one of North Carolina’s most dynamic and fast-growing communities. Home to more than 305,000 residents , the city has grown nearly 8% since 2020, and more than 57% of adults hold a bachelor’s degree or higher. Durham is anchored by Duke University, North Carolina Central University, world-class healthcare institutions, and Research Triangle Park, a 7,000-acre innovation hub that is home to more than 385 companies.

Durham’s quality of life has also earned national attention. Forbes included Raleigh-Durham among the nation’s top 15 communities for quality of life, Livability named Durham one of the best places to live in the United States in 2025, and Food & Wine recognized it as one of “America’s next great food cities.” The community also offers nationally recognized arts and entertainment, diverse neighborhoods, outdoor recreation, and a strong tradition of civic engagement.

This combination of rapid growth, innovation, diversity, and community commitment gives APS’s next leader a meaningful platform for partnership and impact. It also creates increasingly complex animal welfare needs as Durham works to ensure that services remain accessible to animals and the people who care for them.

Want to know more? Visit www.discoverdurham.com.

Benefits

APS offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees, including generous health coverage, retirement contributions, paid time off, and professional development opportunities. We are committed to providing benefits and workplace practices that support employee well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

The Executive Director of Advanced Practice is a strategic and operational leader, responsible for optimizing the delivery of care provided by all Nurse Practitioners (NPs), Physician Assistants (PAs), Certified Nurse Midwives (CNMs), Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs), Genetic Counselors (GC) within LPCH/SMCH Center for Advanced Practice (CAP). The Executive Director fills an executive sponsorship role where they partner with key constituents across the enterprise to represent the Center for Advanced Practice. Leads annual goal development, deployment, and measurement process.

Skills

Uses a systematic process to effectively plan, implement, and evaluate new programs in conjunction with division/service physicians and hospital and clinic leadership.

Serves as the leader, positive role model, and effective liaison for Stanford Medicine Children's Health (SMCH) and key external stakeholders.
Is actively involved with governmental agencies, professional organizations, health policy/advocacy groups to identify and implement best practices in professional practice and pediatric healthcare.

Oversees APP billing practices in conjunction with the Provider Enrollment and Compliance Departments, as well as with physician practices.
Establishes and maintains patient care, human resources, systems, and workflow processes, including the development, review, and annual update of the CAP budget.

Data Collection And Analysis

Human Resources

CAP Leadership Team

Oversees the operations, strategy, and business needs to lead a team CAP leaders to support the clinical and professional practice of advanced practice professionals across the continuum.

Leads strategies to optimize APP contribution to patient access, aligning APP utilization, deployment and practice models with SMCH access initiatives and organizational goals.
Guides the management team to create, maintain, and update staffing models to ensure appropriate staffing across all units and specialties.
Oversees the management team to review all new and replacement APP positions supporting resource stewardship and ensuring patient care needs are met.

Oversees credentialing and privileging competencies for the professional staff and participation in peer review.
Develops and maintains policies and procedures relating to the practice of the APPs.

Collaborates with marketing for both internal and external CAP marketing opportunities.

At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. AI strategy and portfolio leadership

Native AI organization building

Create an engineering culture centered on innovation, responsible experimentation, accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and disciplined production delivery.

Lead AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions from discovery and architecture through engineering, release, adoption, operation, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Product Management and business stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into sequenced, funded, and measurable delivery commitments.
Manage execution across concurrent initiatives while balancing value, speed, quality, security, risk, reliability, and maintainability.
Establish outcome, delivery, quality, adoption, and operational measures; use results to improve priorities and execution.

Define patterns for large language model integration, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent workflow automation, observability, evaluation, and model operations.

Fifteen or more years of progressive software engineering and technology leadership experience.
Seven or more years leading software development organizations, including leaders of engineering teams.
Five or more years delivering AI-enabled applications, machine learning platforms, intelligent automation solutions, or generative AI products.
Demonstrated success creating and scaling a native AI software development organization that moved beyond pilots and experimentation to secure, production-grade solutions.

Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families.

We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. We’re a lifestyle organization, a friend and neighbor, and a trusted partner. Our approach is collaborative, human-centered, and designed with the whole family in mind.

A Blue Star Family is one with an immediate family member — a spouse, parent, or child — actively serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, including the Guard and Reserves. These families face unique challenges: frequent relocations, deployments, career disruption, and isolation. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

We serve with urgency but build trust over time — because change happens at the speed of trust. Whether we’re driving spouse employment, supporting caregivers, or helping communities welcome military families, we strive for upstream solutions.

Who We’re Looking For

Bold thinkers. Fast movers. Smart collaborators. People who want to build, lead, and drive measurable change — and who care deeply about making an impact that matters.

What You’ll Do Here

Solve complex challenges with data, heart, and humility
Build cross-sector partnerships that get things done
Help military families feel at home wherever they live

If you're ready to work in a high-performance, mission-driven environment — and to make life better for those who serve — Blue Star Families is where you belong.

General Description

The Associate Director, Development for the Utah Chapter is responsible for assisting in local fundraising efforts, cultivating donor relationships, and supporting the development of strategic partnerships to support the chapter’s financial sustainability and growth. This role partners closely with the Chapter Executive Director and the national Development team to align local fundraising strategies with Blue Star Families’ mission and organizational goals.

The Associate Director will steward a portfolio of individual, corporate, and foundation donors and support grant writing and reporting in collaboration with the national team.

While this role is remote, periodic out-of-town, overnight travel is an essential function. In-person time is critical to how we work — enabling deep collaboration, team alignment, creative problem-solving, and a shared sense of purpose. Team members are expected to travel several times per year for offsites, planning sessions, and company-wide gatherings. These events are essential for contributing to team outcomes, building trust across the organization, and staying aligned in a distributed environment. Participation in these in-person gatherings is a required part of the role and integral to successful performance in our remote-first organization.

The Associate Director must reside in the local community the Chapter serves. Preference will be given to candidates who have resided in the designated Chapter community for a minimum of the past three years.

Assist the Executive Director with the local fundraising strategy to meet or exceed chapter revenue goals.
Meet or exceed an annual fundraising goal of at least $100,000.
Build, qualify, and actively manage a portfolio of at least 30 new major gift prospects (distinct from existing pipelines), with responsibility for identifying, cultivating, and advancing these individuals through the full donor lifecycle toward solicitation and long-term engagement
Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with individual donors, corporate sponsors, and foundations.
Collaborate with the Executive Director and national Development team to identify and pursue funding opportunities aligned with chapter programs and goals.
Collaborate with the Executive Director on donor recognition and ensure consistent, high-quality communication with funders and supporters.
Support the development and execution of donor engagement events and activities.
Maintain accurate donor records and activity tracking in CRM (e.g., Salesforce).
Assist with grant proposal writing and reporting.
Partner with local program staff to align fundraising with community impact.
Represent Blue Star Families at Chapter sponsored events, community events, and networking opportunities to elevate the chapter’s visibility and mission.
Perform other duties as assigned

Minimum 5-7 years of relevant experience in fundraising for a nonprofit organization
Demonstrated success in individual giving, corporate sponsorships, and/or grant writing.
Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
Self-starter with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Experience with CRM software (e.g., Salesforce).
Local travel requirements required outside of your home office will be up to 40% or less depending on business needs.
Ability to travel out of town overnight several times per year for staff offsites, planning retreats, and company-wide events. These gatherings are essential for connection, brainstorming, and staying strategically aligned across teams. Participation is required as a core part of the role.
May be required to work nights, weekends, and holidays as necessary to carry out key job functions.

Desired Experience, Skills & Background

Bachelor’s degree preferred
Knowledge of the military family experience
Familiarity with membership-driven organizations

More About Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families empowers military and Veteran families to thrive by connecting them with their civilian neighbors — both people and organizations — to create strong communities of mutual support. We believe we're all stronger when we take care of one another.

Our groundbreaking research is raising the nation's awareness of the unique challenges of military family life. With the help of neighbors across the country, Blue Star Families is overcoming the isolation and alienation of frequent moves, deployments, and reduced support from the government. Students are our top priority.

The Executive Director of Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) provides enterprise-wide financial leadership for Stanford Medicine Children's Health. This role will oversee and implement annual updates to the long-range financial plan, partnering closely with strategy, service lines, and operational leaders throughout the organization. In addition, the Executive Director will oversee labor productivity reporting and analysis, external benchmarking, and new financial reporting to allow for deeper insights into the enterprise financial performance and operational efficiency. This position will be a key advisor to senior leadership and will be responsible for preparing financial updates that are presented to the Board of Directors.

Executive presence with the ability to influence and partner with senior leaders.

Job Description

As CohnReznick grows, so do our career opportunities. As one of the nation’s top professional services firms, CohnReznick creates rewarding careers in advisory, assurance, and tax with team members who value innovation and collaboration in everything they do!

CohnReznick helps organizations optimize performance, manage risk, and maximize value through CohnReznick LLP (assurance services) and CohnReznick Advisory LLC (advisory and tax services). Together, the firm provides leaders with deep industry knowledge and relationships, solutions to address clients’ unique business goals and risks, and insight on how emerging market forces can drive opportunity. With offices nationwide, the firm serves organizations around the world as an independent member of Nexia.

We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a Director/Managing Director, AI Software Development
to support our Global Digital & CyberSecurity
practice.

CohnReznick is a hybrid firm and most of our professionals are located within a commutable distance to one of our offices. This position is considered remote which means it does not require job duties be performed within proximity of a CohnReznick office location. However, as a remote employee, you may be required to be present at a CohnReznick office with scheduled notice for client work, team meetings, or trainings.

YOUR TEAM.

The Director / Managing Director, AI Software Development is a senior technology leader responsible for establishing and leading CohnReznick's software engineering capability. This position defines the vision, strategy, operating model, talent plan, architecture, and delivery approach for AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions across the firm.

The position is accountable for building a high-performing AI-native software development organization capable of delivering proprietary technology assets that create sustainable competitive advantage. The leader oversees the design, development, deployment, and operation of AI-powered applications, intelligent automation solutions, agentic workflows, and client-facing digital products.

This is not a traditional application-development leadership role. The successful candidate must have personally built and scaled a native AI software team from inception through production delivery, including recruiting specialized talent, establishing engineering and governance standards, and delivering secure applications with measurable business impact.

WHY COHNREZNICK?

At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. Whether it’s working alongside your peers to solve a client challenge, or volunteering together at the local food bank, there are so many ways to find your “why” at the firm.

We believe it’s important to balance work with everyday life – and make time for enjoyment and fun. We invest in a robust Total Rewards package that includes everything from generous PTO, a flexible work environment, expanded parental leave, extensive learning & development, and even paid time off for employees to volunteer.

YOUR ROLE.

Responsibilities Include But Not Limited To

AI strategy and portfolio leadership

Define and execute a multi-year AI software engineering strategy aligned with firm business and technology objectives.
Establish the vision, roadmap, investment priorities, and operating model for the GDC AI development capability.
Identify opportunities to create proprietary software assets that improve client service, quality, efficiency, growth, and professional experience.
Advise executive leaders and governance forums on opportunities, investments, risks, dependencies, and portfolio performance.

Native AI organization building

Recruit, organize, develop, and retain a multidisciplinary team of AI engineers, software engineers, machine learning engineers, technical leads, and architects.
Define job architecture, role expectations, career paths, leadership spans, technical communities, and talent-development practices for the AI engineering function.
Create an engineering culture centered on innovation, responsible experimentation, accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and disciplined production delivery.
Build a sustainable talent pipeline and develop future engineering leaders.

Product and solution delivery

Lead AI-enabled products, platforms, and solutions from discovery and architecture through engineering, release, adoption, operation, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Product Management and business stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into sequenced, funded, and measurable delivery commitments.
Manage execution across concurrent initiatives while balancing value, speed, quality, security, risk, reliability, and maintainability.
Establish outcome, delivery, quality, adoption, and operational measures; use results to improve priorities and execution.

Architecture, engineering, and operations

Establish development standards, reference architectures, engineering frameworks, reusable components, testing practices, and technical quality controls.
Define patterns for large language model integration, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent workflow automation, observability, evaluation, and model operations.
Implement modern cloud-native engineering, DevSecOps, CI/CD, API, integration, reliability, incident-management, and lifecycle-management practices.
Promote reuse, platform leverage, technical-debt management, and reduction of unnecessary technology redundancy.

Governance, risk, and stakeholder leadership

Embed security, privacy, legal, regulatory, records-management, data-governance, and responsible AI requirements throughout the development lifecycle.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Data & Analytics, Risk, Legal, and other control functions to govern design and deployment decisions.
Communicate complex technical matters in clear business terms and build trusted relationships with executives, professionals, clients, vendors, and strategic partners.
Drive adoption, change leadership, knowledge transfer, and transparent reporting of progress, risks, decisions, and realized value.

The duties listed are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. They are not an exhaustive list of every responsibility, duty, or skill required. Responsibilities may change based on business needs.

Your Experience.

The successful candidate will have:

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Fifteen or more years of progressive software engineering and technology leadership experience.
Seven or more years leading software development organizations, including leaders of engineering teams.
Five or more years delivering AI-enabled applications, machine learning platforms, intelligent automation solutions, or generative AI products.
Demonstrated success creating and scaling a native AI software development organization that moved beyond pilots and experimentation to secure, production-grade solutions.
Proven delivery of enterprise-grade software products and platforms in complex, regulated, or high-trust environments.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and a blended workforce of employees, contractors, and strategic partners.

Technical and delivery expertise

Generative AI, large language models, agentic architectures, retrieval-augmented generation, AI evaluation, observability, and model operations.
Cloud-native software development, enterprise application architecture, APIs, integration patterns, data platforms, and analytics ecosystems.
DevSecOps, CI/CD, automated testing, software supply-chain controls, production reliability, and secure development lifecycle practices.
Responsible AI, AI governance, privacy, security, model risk, data governance, and human oversight.
Product-oriented delivery using measurable outcomes, iterative development, user feedback, adoption measures, and value realization.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Business, or a related field.
Leadership experience in professional services, financial services, regulated industries, or enterprise B2B software.
Experience with Microsoft Azure AI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot technologies, and modern AI engineering frameworks.
Relevant credentials in AI, cloud architecture, software engineering, cybersecurity, or product delivery.
Experience commercializing proprietary software or creating client-facing digital products and technology-enabled services.

Studies have shown that we are less likely to apply to jobs unless we meet every single qualification. At CohnReznick, we are dedicated to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. You may be just the right candidate for this or one of our other roles.
